replacement.title: Replace high support after entry
replacement.objective: Fill a changed high support role without crowding the puck carrier.
replacement.briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net. After F2 receives the entry pass, YOU are on the wall side of F2 and F3 supports lower in the zone. A1 and A2 defend inside while D1 is nearer the blue line. The next support job depends on F2 and those defenders.
cues: F2 owns the puck after the stated entry pass.
YOU are the high support option.

sources.title: U15 / U18 Practice Plan — High Performance Practice 4
sources.use: Supports the stated coaching principle. The setup, alternatives and suggested answers are original experimental coaching synthesis, not source-certified.

replacement.limits: Static experimental practice scene. Positions are examples and do not prove timing, execution, possession outcome, or a universal team system; coaching responses are ungraded.

questions.prompt: After the entry pass, which Navy player is the carrier?
questions.explanation: The setup assigns possession to F2 after the entry pass.

questions.prompt: Which two details matter when filling high support?

options.text: A high support spot chosen without checking F2’s lane

questions.explanation: Support follows the carrier and coverage; a fixed spot can crowd or disconnect the play.

options.text: Find F2 and the inside coverage

questions.explanation: Finding F2 and the inside coverage can overlap with skating to the new lane; a player keeps scanning while moving. The final re-check still comes last because it depends on where the play has actually gone once the lane is offered.

questions.prompt: Move YOU into a high-slot support example after F2 receives.
questions.explanation: This gives F2 a higher connection while keeping the defenders visible.

questions.prompt: F2 loses the puck to A2. What takes priority?

options.text: Re-read the transition and recover toward the dangerous lane
Assume the entry is still controlled

questions.explanation: Possession changed, so the role changes before the old support route is continued.

questions.prompt: Which support space did YOU fill, and what route does it leave F2?
questions.explanation: A separated high-slot lane gives F2 a visible outlet or room to carry. If Gold closes it, re-offer from another reachable angle.

reasons.issue: cues[1] read "YOU is the high support option.", a subject-verb agreement error (lesson 4, the single most common defect class). The prior repair receipt (historical-checks.json repairReceipts[0], status applied-awaiting-independent-recheck) already fixed the identical "YOU is" error inside the briefing (v1: "YOU is near the right blue line" -> v2: "YOU are on the wall side of F2") but left the same error standing in cues[1], confirming this packet’s standing lesson that a partial grammar fix does not clear the whole scene and that prior pass labels are not proof.
reasons.change: Corrected cues[1] to "YOU are the high support option." Because this is a scene-level field, every linked question’s content hash changes.
reasons.evidence: v2 scene cues array index 1; AUTHORING-CONTRACT.md mandates all-caps YOU with natural subject-verb agreement ("YOU have", "YOU are").

reasons.issue: Q3 is a sequence question whose explanation ("The support lane is useful only if it remains reachable from F2.") did not disclose that the first two steps (find F2/coverage; offer a separated high lane) can overlap, contrary to AUTHORING-CONTRACT.md’s explicit instruction not to imply an artificial look/decide/execute order for reads that can overlap (lesson 11).
reasons.change: Kept the same three-item sequence and answer key (a,b,c). Rewrote the explanation to state that scanning for F2 and the inside coverage can happen while skating into the new lane, and that the final re-check still comes last because it depends on where the play has actually gone once the lane is offered.
reasons.evidence: AUTHORING-CONTRACT.md: "Scanning and moving can overlap. Do not imply a player must stop scanning, wait to look for pressure, or follow an artificial ‘look, decide, execute’ order for every read."
